metadata.title: The Jacobian Lens
metadata.purpose: Lay out exactly what the Jacobian lens is, prove it beats the older lenses, then name the single-token blind spot the paper ships its own patches for.
metadata.gate: GATE P — moot (Kokoro free); audio not yet generated

props.command: Anthropic says it found a way to read what a model is about to say — at every layer, before it says anything. Walk me through the Jacobian lens paper, and tell me where the trick breaks.
props.runningText: composer types the ask — no narration

beats.narration_text: July 2026. Anthropic publishes a paper the length of a book, built around one instrument. Before we trust any reading it takes, we look at the instrument.
A transformer builds its answer layer by layer, in a running scratch vector called the residual stream. The question is what's written there, mid-stack — long before the output.

graphic.description: token column rising through a layer stack; probe arrow at layer L

beats.new_visual_element: residual stream layer stack with probe arrow

beats.narration_text: The Jacobian lens asks, for every word in the vocabulary: if the model were about to say this word, which direction in this layer's activations would push it harder? One gradient. One vector per word.

graphic.description: gradient arrows flowing back from output distribution to layer L; one vector per vocabulary token materializes

beats.new_visual_element: gradient arrows from output to layer L; vocabulary vectors appearing

beats.narration_text: Project the actual activations onto those directions and you get a ranking — the ten words this layer, at this token, is most about. That ranked list is the readout. That's the whole instrument.

graphic.description: activation vector projected onto gradient directions; top-10 word list pops out ranked

beats.narration_text: It has two older siblings. The logit lens asks what the model would say if it stopped here. The tuned lens learns a correction first. The Jacobian lens asks a different question — not what would you say, but what are you thinking about.

left.label: Logit lens / Tuned lens
left.note: What would you say if you stopped here?

right.label: Jacobian lens
right.note: What are you thinking about right now?

beats.new_visual_element: divergence card: continuation question vs concept question

beats.narration_text: On a counting prompt, the middle layers read out numbers. On a translation prompt, the target language. On a poem, the rhyme it hasn't written yet. Concepts, not continuations.

graphic.description: rebuild Fig 3 essence: six mini-prompts, midlayer readouts appearing over tokens; skeptic caption bottom

beats.skeptic_caption: Selected examples — the quantitative test is next.
beats.new_visual_element: six prompt types × midlayer readout words

beats.narration_text: Head to head on recovering the model's unspoken intermediate concepts, the Jacobian lens beats both older lenses across all six prompt families. Not by a little. That's Figure fifty-two, and it's the paper's license to use this tool for everything else.

graphic.description: Fig 52 as animated bars: pass@k AUC for intermediate-concept recovery, J-lens vs logit vs tuned, six distributions. Values from img_c983850908bf60d9.png.
graphic.factcheck_note: FACTCHECK.md required before review cut. Typo-panel values need paper-text verification before narration 'all six' is locked.

beats.new_visual_element: Fig 52 animated bar comparison — six prompt families

beats.narration_text: And it's not just reading. In a riddle whose hidden middle step is 'spider,' swap the spider coordinates for ant — and the model's answer about legs follows the swap. The lens finds directions the model actually uses.

graphic.description: readout word 'spider' lifted out; 'ant' inserted; output answer flips. Spider→ant pair from paper Fig 13/15.

beats.narration_text: The paper runs this recipe at every layer, every token, across the Claude model family — and publishes the interactive readouts so you can scrub them yourself.
beats.credit: Gurnee*, Sofroniew* et al., 'Verbalizable Representations Form a Global Workspace in Language Models', Transformer Circuits Thread, Anthropic, July 2026 — §2.1 methods figure, reproduced for educational criticism.
beats.new_visual_element: paper's own §2.1 methods figure (computing / reading / intervening)

build.suggested: find: paper's own §2.1 methods figure (computing / reading / intervening)

beats.narration_text: So far, so clean. Now the part the press release won't lead with.

props.caption: Three steps — two solid, one open.

beats.new_visual_element: step-stream pivot card: third step active

beats.narration_text: The lens computes one vector per vocabulary token. 'Blackmail' is two tokens. So in the paper's own blackmail case study, the instrument registers the act only as the fragment 'black' — a reader has to finish the word.

graphic.description: 'blackmail' splits into black|mail tokens; lens vector attaches only to 'black'; 'mail' fades

beats.narration_text: The appendix ships two patches. A template lens, for words you can enumerate in advance. And an oracle lens that decodes whole phrases — at one email sign-off it reads, quote, 'blackmail him by revealing.' Both find content the main instrument misses.

graphic.description: two patch-lenses appear: template lens decoding 'blackmail' whole; oracle lens emitting phrase 'blackmail him by revealing'

beats.skeptic_caption: If the patches see more, the J-space is a slice — not the whole workspace.
beats.new_visual_element: two patches: template + oracle lenses find what J-lens misses

beats.narration_text: Here's the honest label. The instrument works, the causal tests back it, and it is still blind to every thought longer than one token. Hold both.

props.title: The J-lens reads the model's verbalizable thoughts

beats.narration_text: The verdict. One gradient per word, at every layer. It out-reads the older lenses, and the swap experiments prove the directions do real work. But it cannot see a thought longer than one token, and every reading so far comes from one vendor's models.

artifactLines: One gradient per vocabulary word, at every layer.
Beats the older lenses at recovering unspoken concepts.
Swaps prove the directions are load-bearing.
Blind to multi-token concepts — 'blackmail' reads as 'black'.
Every result so far: one vendor's models.

beats.narration_text: Your turn. Ask your model to walk the three lenses with one worked example — and to name the question none of them can answer.

props.command: Explain the difference between the logit lens, the tuned lens, and the Jacobian lens to me with one worked example — then tell me which single-token limitation each one has, and which of my questions none of them could answer.
